title: Campaign: connectomes, how reliable are connectome measurements?
abstract: Subcampaign of 'what do connectomes reveal about how nervous systems are built?'. Scope: Errors and biases in the connectome data themselves: synapse detection and count noise, missing partners, proofreading and annotation artefacts. 4 papers. Status: supported. Left-right connection counts in FlyWire vary as 2.5 times Poisson plus an 11% proportional part (26% between hemibrain and FlyWire); the excess comes from clusters of nearby T-bars, and 2 um presynaptic clusters explain the left-right count dispersion. Only 44.7% of FlyWire synapses have a postsynaptic side attached to a proofread neuron; correcting for this reduces the variance of the shared neuron gain by 13-28%, but the gain remains in 115 of 124 tests.
